title: The Chart in a Terminal: A Steady Signal Stays Steady and a Spike Stays a Spike

questions.question: A signal is 5 plus or minus 1e-6. The chart scales the range to the data. What does it show?
options: A storm: the range is 2e-6 wide
questions.explanation: The noise fills the chart. It marked 11 of 13 rows.

questions.question: What does min_span do?
options: Makes the range at least that wide, centred on the data
Sets the step of the ticks
questions.explanation: A steady signal is a flat line. With a span of 1 the same signal marked one row.

questions.question: Why is the spike in row 1 and not row 0?
options: The range has 5 percent of room above the highest value

questions.question: What does row_for do with a value above the range?
options: Keeps it inside the chart: row 0
Returns a row past the top
questions.explanation: row_for(99) on a range of 0 to 10 was row 0.

questions.question: Why are labels put on tick rows rather than on every row?
options: A label says something only where a tick is
questions.explanation: The value at that row is a nice number. The 13 rows had 3 labels, on nice numbers.

questions.question: What is min_span a choice about?
options: What counts as steady for this signal
questions.explanation: 0.1 suits a temperature and not a microvolt. The chart cannot know the scale at which a signal stops being interesting.
